Description: Constructs that reference at least 35 distinct receivers — a fan-out / coupling detector with an ABSOLUTE threshold, so a construct's verdict depends only on that construct. Counts distinct RECEIVERS (qualifier, falling back to token), not call sites: threading one helper through a wide function does not trip it, talking to 35 different things does. The threshold was corpus-relative until mache-ce0bcd (n >= 5 AND n > 3x the project mean). That design needed two prior patches just to keep its statistic honest — markdown backtick spans dragged the mean 9.79 -> 5.08 (mache-50e939), the vendored corpus dragged it again (mache-f41b43) — and was still wrong a third way: the mean was computed over 5,039 callers while the rule reports on only 2,420, so test-code fan-out set the bar for production code (34.31 where its own definition implied 21.56, leaving the gate far more permissive than intended). A relative bar also couples every verdict to unrelated files and cannot be held steady by a committed ratchet baseline. 35 is calibrated to reproduce mache's own findings exactly at the moment of the switch — a judgement call, not a law — and is meant to be tuned per project via --min-metric or a rules-dir override. Test constructs, generated files and vendored trees are excluded as noise.
Query:
WITH fanout AS (
				-- Exclude the engine's file-level sentinel caller_ids
				-- (prefix '_file_level:'). Those are synthetic node_ids
				-- the engine uses to mark file-level fn-value refs
				-- (mache-02r9) as alive without polluting per-construct
				-- callee counts. Counting them here would attribute the
				-- file-level refs to a 'caller' that isn't a real
				-- construct, inflating fan_out_skew with virtual rows.
				--
				-- Metric: COUNT DISTINCT qualifier per referrer.
				-- Qualifier is the LHS of the selector_expression at
				-- the ref site (per LLO BindingRecord.qualifier, T8.7).
				-- Counting distinct qualifiers — receiver/package
				-- origins — distinguishes orchestration (calls across
				-- many packages) from projection (N method calls on
				-- one receiver, N distinct tokens but ONE qualifier).
				--
				-- Pre-T8.7 records and tree-sitter mention rows have
				-- empty qualifier; the COALESCE falls back to token
				-- so the metric degrades gracefully to the pre-T8.7
				-- behavior on those records (no regression for legacy
				-- .dbs without the qualifier field).
				SELECT referrer_node_id AS caller_id,
				       COUNT(DISTINCT COALESCE(NULLIF(qualifier, ''), token)) AS n
				FROM v_refs
				WHERE referrer_node_id NOT LIKE '_file_level:%%'
				GROUP BY referrer_node_id
			)
			-- This rule carried a corpus-relative bar (n > 3x the project
			-- mean) until mache-ce0bcd, and needed a mean-scoping CTE to
			-- keep that bar honest: markdown backtick spans dragged the
			-- mean 9.79 -> 5.08 (mache-50e939), and the vendored corpus
			-- dragged it again (mache-f41b43). Two patches to defend a
			-- statistic, and it was still wrong a third way -- the mean
			-- was taken over 5,039 callers while the rule only REPORTS on
			-- 2,420, so test-code fan-out set the bar for production code
			-- (34.31 where its own definition implied 21.56). An absolute
			-- threshold has no statistic to distort, so all three go away.
			SELECT COALESCE(n.source_file, '') AS source_id,
			       f.caller_id AS node_id,
			       0 AS start_byte,
			       0 AS end_byte,
			       0 AS start_row,
			       0 AS start_col,
			       f.n AS metric
			FROM fanout f
			JOIN nodes n ON n.id = f.caller_id
			-- Construct directory is the parent of the source node.
			-- Match against ctor.name so the test-prefix filter checks
			-- the construct name directly, not arbitrary substrings of
			-- the path. ctor will be NULL for top-level callers (rare);
			-- the LEFT JOIN keeps those rows so the test-prefix filter
			-- only excludes when we positively identify a test name.
			LEFT JOIN nodes ctor ON ctor.id = n.parent_id
			WHERE f.n >= 5
			  AND COALESCE(ctor.name, '') NOT LIKE 'Test%%'
			  AND COALESCE(ctor.name, '') NOT LIKE 'Benchmark%%'
			  AND COALESCE(ctor.name, '') NOT LIKE 'Example%%'
			  AND COALESCE(ctor.name, '') NOT LIKE 'Fuzz%%'
			  -- Generated dispatchers (capnp / protobuf / *_generated /
			  -- *.gen) have intentionally wide fan-out; flagging them
			  -- buries real findings under generated-code noise.
			  AND COALESCE(n.source_file, '') NOT LIKE '%%.capnp.go'
			  AND COALESCE(n.source_file, '') NOT LIKE '%%.pb.go'
			  AND COALESCE(n.source_file, '') NOT LIKE '%%_generated.go'
			  AND COALESCE(n.source_file, '') NOT LIKE '%%.gen.go'
			  -- Go test files: test helpers (RunSuite, runParity,
			  -- setup, realWriteBack) legitimately call many things
			  -- to build fixtures. The Test*/Benchmark*/Example*/Fuzz*
			  -- per-construct filter above doesn't catch helpers
			  -- with non-test names, so add a per-file filter to
			  -- match god_file.
			  AND COALESCE(n.source_file, '') NOT LIKE '%%_test.go'
			  -- The %%_test.go filter above is Go-only. Rust marks tests by
			  -- ATTRIBUTE and colocates them in the production file, so no path
			  -- predicate can see them — and test helpers are exactly the shape this
			  -- rule false-positives on, calling many things to build fixtures.
			  -- Measured on ley-line-open/rs: 90 of 176 findings (51%%) were test
			  -- code. Empty on projections without _ast, so inert elsewhere
			  -- (mache-c7d56d).
			  AND f.caller_id NOT IN (SELECT node_id FROM v_test_nodes)
			  -- Vendored corpus is checked in to be PARSED, not maintained
			  -- (mache-f41b43). Stated once now: it used to be duplicated
			  -- into the mean's CTE, which no longer exists.
			  AND COALESCE(n.source_file, '') NOT IN (SELECT source_file FROM v_vendored_files)

			%s
			ORDER BY metric DESC, source_id, node_id
